A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe EDEN. Their text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EDEN benchmark results, runtime measurements, and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, runtime measurements, and main-text and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same tokenizer, pyramid feature fusion, temporal attention, difference embedding, fine-tuning procedure, and training objectives.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including LAVIB, DAVIS, DAIN-HD544p, SNU-FILM, and VIMEO. The corrected SNU-FILM heading does not establish new coverage: Section 4.2 already describes the extreme-motion subset in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VFIFormer, ST-MFNet, AMT, SGM-VFI, VFIMamba, LDMVFI, and LBBDM. Comparator membership in the appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported subset heading from SNU-FILM (Hard) to SNU-FILM (Extreme), aligning it with the existing Section 4.2 description. This is a limited correction to the reported evaluation split; the PDFs do not establish rerunning experiments or changing other settings.

E4.justification: All main-text and appendix analyses are retained, including component ablations, tokenizer scaling, denoising steps, increased frame intervals, matched training-data comparisons, and failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical values, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. The relabeled Table 1 columns retain EDEN's 0.0986 LPIPS and 0.1653 FloLPIPS; Section 4.2 already attributes the 0.0986 result to extreme motion in both versions.

T1.justification: The transformer equations, tokenizer loss, diffusion-path formulation, velocity-field equation, and diffusion objective are identical. No theoretical material is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same method contributions and claims about perceptual performance, large-motion interpolation, and inference efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning temporal attention, resolution generalization, and tokenizer capacity are unchanged. Section 5 and Appendix A.9 retain the fine-detail blurring limitation and proposed decoder explanation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, model dimensions, training budgets, testing hardware, and the printed code-access link are unchanged throughout the main text and appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning, and all 69 numbered references are unchanged.

P1.justification: Text edits are confined to the SNU-FILM subset heading and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. Narrative prose and section organization, including the appendix, are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1's final benchmark heading changes from Hard to Extreme, with minor local layout adjustments. No figures or tables are added, removed, or relocated; appendix displays are identical.

improvement.justification: v1's Table 1 labels results as SNU-FILM Hard while Section 4.2 describes them as Extreme. v2 corrects the heading, resolving an internal inconsistency that could mislead benchmark comparisons. This improves reporting accuracy, while the method, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
